POSITIVE, first accepted Area 2 family. 32 cost-of-entry + race-structure features from BR position (+ election frequency + office holders), 88.0% reach = the decidable population. Pooled 0.8695->0.8748 (+0.0053), decidable 0.8172->0.8247 (+0.0075), PR 0.8844->0.8891. FORWARD FLAT at 0.8912 (+0.0000) in every variant, which is the one caution. Family alone 0.8177. Ablation: minus holder block 0.8730/0.8221, holder block only 0.8724/0.8213 — the blocks are near-redundant and holder alone carries most of the lift. Holder block KEPT by decision (Tristan): holder records are written during a term so they predate filing deadlines and an incumbent is almost certainly real. Recorded caveat: the columns are POSITION-level (holders per seat, not whether this user holds it), and where BR has no holder record 99.4%% of rows also lack BR candidacy data (corroboration 25.1%% vs 67.9%%), so the block is largely nested in the coverage-proxy channel; the person-level version of the argument is the parked incumbency feature. Also decided: filing-fee zeros are real (nulls carry unknown separately); pos_is_retention dropped (10 positives). Top importances are holder_count then paperwork_len, tier, has_primary, filing_req_len — the filing FEE ranks near the bottom, so the cost-of-entry hypothesis is not what carries this family.

POSITIVE but small, and a LEAKAGE CHANNEL FOUND. 7 person-level office-holder features matched on (state, first, last) and PIT-gated to terms starting <= signup (a later term is often the one won in the election being predicted). Clean result: pooled 0.8695->0.8727 (+0.0032), decidable 0.8172->0.8217 (+0.0045), forward 0.8912->0.8976 (+0.0064) — forward improves, unlike the position family. Family alone 0.5726. 16.5% are office holders at signup, 9.7% already hold the seat they are running for. LEAKAGE: the first run scored 0.8893/0.8452/0.9127 and inc_name_ambiguity (count of holder records sharing the name+state) dominated importances at 0.081, ~50x everything else. Removing it and inc_match_is_unique drops the lift from +0.0198 to +0.0032, so 85%% of the apparent gain was name commonness. MECHANISM: the corroboration label is built by entity-resolution NAME MATCHING against BR/TS/DDHQ, so a common name is easier to match to a candidacy and therefore more likely labelled corroborated — label-construction leakage, not reality. The two columns stay in the artifact as match-precision diagnostics and are excluded from the model via exp_family --exclude. GENERAL WARNING: any name-derived feature can leak through this channel, which likely also touches the name-plausibility family. Top clean importances: days_to_term_end, holds_same_position, term_ends_within_1y, years_in_office. Replace with the governed is_incumbent flag when the BR rebuild lands.

Answers where to cut the training window for 2026 targets. Test set held fixed = frozen forward split (2026+ completed, n=1,181, base 0.517). Hard cutoffs get WORSE as they get shorter: 2025+ 0.8894 (current), 2025Q2+ 0.8778, 2025H2 0.8648, 2025Q4-only 0.7165. Volume beats recency decisively, so do NOT cut to Q4. Including 2024 is neutral (0.8884). WINNER: keep everything from 2024 and apply exponential recency weights, half-life 120d -> 0.8950 / PR 0.9136, i.e. +0.0056 over the current window, which is more than the entire BR position feature family delivered (+0.0053) for a one-line change. Half-life 240d 0.8933, 480d 0.8919, so the gain is monotone in recency emphasis over this range. CALIBRATION BONUS: mean predicted vs actual 0.517 goes from 0.556 (overpredicts 3.9pp on 2025+) to 0.515 with hl=120d, essentially exact on this slice. CAVEAT: n=1,181 and it is the short-lead-time selected slice, so deltas around 0.005 are within noise (the Q4 collapse is not), and calibration on this slice does not prove calibration on the long-lead-time in-cycle population.

Blind web verification of 150 named label=0 users, 30/score-quintile, official filings+certified results. NON-MONOTONE: only the top bin separates (0.75); bins 0-3 flat ~0.36-0.52 and the LOWEST bin is 2nd highest. So the score ranks corroboration, not realness, inside the negative class. Implies ~80pct of the pool is really real and corroboration misses ~26pct of real candidates. CAVEATS: 14 rows budget-limited/access-blocked (bin0 worst: 7); plain NOT_FOUND counted not-real, so bin estimates are floors; canceled-unopposed and write-in races structurally unverifiable.

DATA-2238. Anatomy is coded from verifier notes, which exist only for the sweep wave, so the shares describe the flagged slice. DATA-2238 item 5. ANSWER: NO, in-cycle rows cannot enter training on observed labels. 88% sit 61-90d from their election where only 8.5-11% of eventual BR corroborations have arrived; admitting them would inject ~9k mostly-mislabeled zeros. A maturity-gated rule admits 24 rows, so there is nothing cheap here. The curve's real use is in-cycle base-rate correction, not training augmentation.

DATA-2241 item 4. Calibrated against BOTH corroboration (the training label) and expected realness (PU-weighted), because consumers read the score as realness and the two diverge at the bottom. Cohorts are mature by construction; the live in-cycle population cannot be calibration-verified at all, so the lead-time overlap metric is how far any transfer has to reach.

DATA-2241 item 2. AUC is not comparable across subsets (moves with base rate and n), so every figure carries a bootstrap CI and its base rate. Differences are only claimed where a subset CI excludes the pooled AUC.
